## Summary for the Library

**Why NO_ENTRY:** The pool contained three candidates, but none proposed any harness modifications. All diffed as identical to the base. The variation in rollout outputs (inv1 produced "unknown"; dom1 and agg1 produced "23") reflects stochastic LLM behavior on a fixed harness, not evidence of what harness edits help.

The selection chose agg1 not because of any edit, but because it delivered "23" efficiently (65,921 tokens) and matched base's output, while inv1 diverged to "unknown" on the same code. This demonstrates that repeated runs of an identical harness can produce different quality outputs, but cannot show which harness *change* caused better behavior—there were no changes to measure. Future work should not treat adoption as signal for harness edits when the entire candidate pool held the harness constant.
